notes: 2026 brackets are from the official 2026 Form ND-1ES (SFN 28709, 12-2025) tax rate schedules.
North Dakota starts from federal taxable income (after the federal standard or itemized deduction and the QBI deduction), so no separate state standard deduction or exemption is applied here.

ND adjustments not modeled: exclusion of U.S. obligation interest, 40% long-term capital gain exclusion, Social Security and military retirement exclusions, and state income tax add-back for itemizers.
Credits not modeled: marriage penalty credit, credit for income tax paid to another state, and others.

seDeduction.note: Federal taxable income already reflects the deductible half of SE tax; no ND add-back.

seHealthInsurance.note: Inherited through federal taxable income; no ND add-back.

retirementContributions.note: SEP/solo 401(k) deductions reduce federal taxable income and flow through.

qbi.note: Because ND starts from federal taxable income (Form 1040 line 15), the federal QBI deduction is retained; ND has no QBI add-back.

localIncomeTax.note: North Dakota cities and counties do not levy income taxes.

estimatedTax.threshold: Required only if all apply: you must pay federal estimated tax for 2026; your 2025 ND net tax liability was $1,000 or more; you expect to owe $1,000 or more for 2026 after ND withholding; and withholding will be less than the smaller of 90% of the 2026 liability or 100% of the 2025 liability
estimatedTax.safeHarbor: Pay the smaller of 90% of the 2026 ND net tax liability (66 2/3% for qualified farmers) or 100% of the 2025 liability; underpayments accrue 12% annual interest.

businessCosts.llcFormationFee: $135 registration (Articles of Organization), North Dakota Secretary of State.
businessCosts.annualReportFee: $50 annual report, due November 15 each year.
